findings.text: Main handler do_machine_check is provided for vector code to invoke with interrupted CPU state, coordinating local and broadcast handling and selecting panic, deferred task action, or resume.
Legacy handlers pentium_machine_check with winchip_machine_check plus empty inline fallbacks in the shared header allow dispatch by platform flags.

Exposed helpers intel_clear_lmce with mce_intel_feature_clear with cmci_clear with cmci_disable_bank with cmci_reenable support teardown and restart, each paired with an inert shared header fallback when unsupported.
Exposed configuration points mcheck_cpu_clear with mcheck_enable with mcheck_init with mc_poll_banks with mc_poll_banks_default allow boot and hotplug and polling code to configure handling.
Storm query mce_get_storm_mode is offered as a constant false fallback and separately as a per-CPU poll mode reader, letting timer logic adapt without threshold knowledge.
Four vector definitions cover kernel entry and user entry and unified FRED entry and unified raw entry, where unified forms inspect privilege and forward to the matching kernel or user helper.

Kernel wrapper preserves debug state and rejects user state in debug builds and consults crashing CPU state when initialized, bracketing the main handler with nonmaskable transitions, while user wrapper uses user transitions with the same debug preservation.

Overall exception flow moves from platform dispatch through information gathering and fatality assessment into local or coordinated bank scanning and state clearing and rendezvous completion and tainting and recovery triage and final status clearing, with fatal observations diverting to panic at defined checkpoints.

Locality defaults to local and is refined from status for covered vendors, where local fatal observations panic immediately while broadcast observations enter start and end rendezvous that can upgrade to panic based on combined severity.

Missing restart validity forces task termination intent, while user faults defer to resumable task work selected by address usability and kernel faults attempt fixup or copyin deferral when flagged recoverable and secure guest faults poison the backing page and resume.

Repeated handling for different user pages is treated as unrecoverable and task work is queued at most once per chain, with several fatal combinations ending in panic including local fatal and broadcast fatal and repeated fatal discovery and failed kernel fixup.

Periodic polling uses a global base interval plus per-CPU next interval and timer, where each expiry polls when capable and halves the interval when logged errors remain and doubles it otherwise within floor and rounded ceiling bounds.

Timer arming is suppressed when corrected error ignoring is configured or the interval is zero, while storm mode overrides adaptation and rearms at a fixed one second cadence without updating the stored interval.

Timer objects are created pinned to the CPU and started from the global interval, with deletion walking online CPUs synchronously and restart recreating polling on every CPU before scheduling background processing.

CMCI teardown checks support once then iterates all banks, where single bank disable validates ownership before touching hardware and clears enable and ownership and ends storm tracking when threshold matches the storm value.
Discovery lock is taken with interrupts saved across CMCI bank loops and single bank updates, keeping enable clearing and ownership changes atomic against concurrent discovery and interrupts.
Sysfs mutex serializes bank value changes and corrected error ignoring toggles and CMCI disabled toggles and polling interval changes around timer deletion and per-CPU updates and global restart.

Suspend and shutdown and resume callbacks are grouped in a syscore operations table referenced by a syscore registration object, linking power transitions to error reporting control and CPU reinitialization.
Machine check bus carries identical bus and device names and anchors a per-CPU table of device pointers plus a mask of initialized CPUs, with a release callback that frees the device object.

Per-CPU attribute set exposes polling interval and corrected error ignoring and CMCI disabled controls backed by global configuration storage, alongside timeout and logging controls and optional legacy trigger, terminated by null.

Device lifecycle creates at most one object per CPU and registers it and attaches global attributes then per-bank attributes, and on failure removes what was added in reverse and unregisters, while removal detaches attributes and unregisters and clears the mask and nulls the slot.

Bank sysfs access resolves the bank index from the attribute container and rejects out of range indices and uninitialized banks, displaying the stored control value and on store parsing an unsigned value and updating storage and triggering global restart under lock.

Toggling corrected error ignoring off deletes timers and disables CMCI everywhere while toggling on reenables and restarts timers, and toggling CMCI disabled similarly disables or reenables without touching timers on the disable path.

Suspend and shutdown skip hardware reporting disable on socket shared vendors and otherwise zero initialized bank controls, while resume and CPU restart reinitialize generic state and vendor state and banks and timers where applicable and set the machine check enable bit.

Boot selection supports empty choice enabling the legacy path and keywords off with no_cmci with no_lmce with dont_log_ce with print_all with ignore_ce with bootlog with nobootlog with bios_cmci_threshold with recovery plus a leading digit numeric timeout, with unknown input logged and ignored.

Machine status restart validity flag MCG_STATUS_RIPV drives termination intent while local delivery flag MCG_STATUS_LMCES selects local versus coordinated handling and secure guest flag MCG_STATUS_SEAM_NR selects guest poison handling.

Action required level MCE_AR_SEVERITY selects recovery triage while panic level MCE_PANIC_SEVERITY forces immediate or rendezvous based termination, with recoverable non panicking outcomes recorded as generic recoverable hardware error type HWERR_RECOV_OTHERS and kernel recoverable flag MCE_IN_KERNEL_RECOV and separately copyin flag MCE_IN_KERNEL_COPYIN guiding fixup paths.

Touched hardware comprises global status MSR_IA32_MCG_STATUS with extended control MSR_IA32_MCG_EXT_CTL and local enable MCG_EXT_CTL_LMCE_EN and per-bank control MCA_CTL and per-bank secondary control MSR_IA32_MCx_CTL2 with enable MCI_CTL2_CMCI_EN and threshold mask MCI_CTL2_CMCI_THRESHOLD_MASK and storm value CMCI_STORM_THRESHOLD plus legacy address MSR_IA32_P5_MC_ADDR with legacy type MSR_IA32_P5_MC_TYPE.
Processor control machine check enable X86_CR4_MCE is set during resume and CPU restart to restore reporting after power or hotplug transitions.

Legacy Pentium path reads address and type and logs them and adds a thermal hint when the designated type bit is set and taints, while WinChip path logs a fixed message and taints and unexpected path logs the CPU identity without further state change.

Vendor clearing dispatches Intel to combined local and CMCI clearing and Zhaoxin to local clearing only, where top level clearing is skipped entirely when disabled or when the CPU lacks machine check support.
Early initialization registers three decode notifiers and initializes deferred work and interrupt work facilities for background error processing.
User recovery asserts thread stack and user privilege context before deferring action, preventing kernel stack or privilege confusion when the fault is attributed to user mode.
Per-bank disable helper for cross-CPU calls clears polling membership for the bank then delegates to CMCI bank disabling.
Polling interval store uses the generic unsigned long parser and only triggers a locked global restart when the value actually changed.
